verdicts.tldr: comment.go:53 can never render anything: Plan.Shots is filled only in the arm that branch excludes
verdicts.details: main.go:147-151 is an if/else-if. The realm arm runs whenever len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0, and plan.Shots is assigned only in the else-if (plan.Gnoweb) arm; grep over the package shows one assignment site, main.go:151. Comment's default branch reaches comment.go:53 exactly when p.Gnoweb is true and a realm changed, which is the arm where Shots is nil, so shotGrid returns the empty string and the branch is dead. No empty grid is printed, contrary to the candidate's wording — shotGrid's own len(shots)==0 guard returns "" — and README.md:70 states the split as intended: 'The two are alternatives, never both'. What is left is unreachable code in a brand-new file, which costs the reader nothing at runtime. Fix: drop the shotGrid call at comment.go:53, or fill Plan.Shots in the mixed case and turn the if/else-if into two independent ifs.

verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestChromeShotHasNoDeadline in misc/gnopreview with a stub browser that sleeps: chromeShot must return a deadline error; observe it still blocked after 6s. Plus grep -c timeout-minutes .github/workflows/pr-preview*.yml, all three 0.
verdicts.tldr: a browser that never exits pins the preview runner for six hours and the PR gets no comment
verdicts.details: chromeShot builds exec.Command with no context (shots.go:171-183) and blocks in CombinedOutput at shots.go:184; nothing in the call chain cancels it. cfg.timeout (main.go:76) is passed only to waitReady (main.go:131, main.go:267), so it bounds gnodev readiness and not the browser. All three preview workflows carry zero timeout-minutes, so a stuck Chrome holds the job to the runner's 360-minute default with no preview posted and no log, since the render step's cleanup never runs. Fix: build the command with exec.CommandContext under a per-shot deadline (a minute is generous against the 0.4s a real page takes) and add timeout-minutes to pr-preview.yml.
verdicts.evidence: My run at ecf7af0f2 in a scratch worktree: TestChromeShotHasNoDeadline --- PASS (6.00s), logging 'chromeShot still blocked after 6s on a browser that never exits: no deadline bounds exec.Command' against a /bin/sh stub that only sleeps. grep -c timeout-minutes over pr-preview.yml, pr-preview-publish.yml, pr-preview-cleanup.yml: 0, 0, 0. I also saw a real /opt/google/chrome/chrome still alive past 60s on a page with one stalled subresource, so the hang is not only theoretical. Merge base has no misc/gnopreview and no pr-preview workflows.

verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b4-reach-chromeshot-hang_test.go misc/gnopreview/ && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestChromeShot -v -timeout 5m . — control returns in <1s, the stalled-subresource case is still running at 60s
verdicts.tldr: one external image in a fork's realm markdown holds the preview job open for the runner's full six hours
verdicts.details: A realm page the PR changed is screenshotted by ScreenshotPairs, and its markdown reaches the snapshot unfiltered: AllowSvgDataImage (ext_imgvalidator.go:31-34) returns true for every URI that is not a data: URI, and Crawler.mapURL (crawl.go) returns raw untouched unless it starts with a single '/', so `![](http://host/x.png)` survives into the captured HTML. Chrome then opens that connection; --virtual-time-budget=4000 stops the page's virtual clock but does not bound the process, and chromeShot's exec.Command has no context, so the render step never returns. pr-preview.yml runs on pull_request from any fork and sets no timeout-minutes. Fix: use exec.CommandContext with a deadline in chromeShot, and set timeout-minutes on the preview job.
